title: Pilot Lite: SDK setup + CI wrapper (notes & checklist)
content:
Purpose:
A compact, actionable sketch for a "pilot-lite" SDK onramp that a developer can complete in a small window (~10–30 minutes) and that plugs into CI for PR-level checks. Goal is to reduce time-to-first-success and to bake in minimal telemetry and CI gating so product/eng can iterate safely during early trials.

Scope / audience:
- New devs evaluating Redwood SDK for embedding/generation/chat integrations.
- Growth/solutions engineers running quick POCs with customers.
- Internal squads wanting a low-friction CI guardrail before committing to a full integration.

Outcome (what success looks like):
- Developer can run the quickstart locally and get a sample generation + embedding call ✅
- A CI job exists that validates: lint, small unit test that hits a sandboxed hosted API key (with voicemail fallback), and a snapshot regression on one prompt ✅
- Telemetry contract (basic events) emitted from SDK sample to staging telemetry endpoint ✅
- README + one-liner curl + snippet in major SDK languages (py/ts) included ✅

High-level flow (happy path):
1) Clone repo + checkout pilot-lite branch
2) Create .env with REDWOOD_API_KEY_SANDBOX
3) python -m venv .venv && pip install -r requirements.txt (or npm install)
4) run `./scripts/pilot-lite-start` (wraps env check, token validation, sample call)
5) see sample response and telemetry ping to staging
6) open PR with the sample; CI runs smoke tests and telemetry check

Local quickstart commands (minimal, copy-paste):
- UNIX
  export REDWOOD_API_KEY_SANDBOX=sk-test-___
  git clone git@github.com:redwood-inference/sdk-examples.git
  cd sdk-examples/pilot-lite
  ./scripts/pilot-lite-start

- scripts/pilot-lite-start (rough pseudocode):
  #!/usr/bin/env bash
  set -e
  if [ -z "$REDWOOD_API_KEY_SANDBOX" ]; then echo "set REDWOOD_API_KEY_SANDBOX"; exit 1; fi
  python -m pip install -r requirements.txt
  python examples/pilot_gen.py --prompt "Write a one-sentence summary of Redwood"
  node examples/verify_telemetry.js || echo "telemetry-check skipped"

Sample Python snippet to include in README (single-file):
- examples/pilot_gen.py (concept):
  from redwood import RedwoodClient
  c = RedwoodClient(api_key=os.getenv('REDWOOD_API_KEY_SANDBOX'))
  out = c.generate("Write a haiku about distributed inference")
  print(out.text)

CI overlay (GitHub Actions sketch):
- name: pilot-lite-smoke
  on: [pull_request]
  jobs:
    smoke:
      runs-on: ubuntu-latest
      steps:
        - checkout
        - uses: actions/setup-python@v4
        - run: pip install -r requirements.txt
        - run: python -m pytest tests/test_smoke.py -k pilot_lite --maxfail=1 -q
      env:
        REDWOOD_API_KEY_SANDBOX: ${{ secrets.REDWOOD_API_KEY_SANDBOX }}

CI tests to include (minimal):
- test_smoke.py::test_generation_returns_text (hit sandbox endpoint, assert status & body)
- test_telemetry_ping (mock/stub telemetry endpoint, assert event envelope shape)
- test_snapshot_prompt_regression (compare small deterministic generation under fixed seed)

Telemetry contract (minimum fields - emits to staging ingestion):
- event_type: "pilot_lite.invoke"
- sdk_version: "x.y.z"
- env: "sandbox"
- route: "generate" | "embed"
- duration_ms: <int>
- tokens_in/out: {in: int, out: int}
- success: true|false
- context: {sample_prompt_hash: str}  # can be a hash not full prompt

Error classes & developer guidance:
- INVALID_KEY (400): tell user to check env var name; include a one-liner to mask and revoke keys
- RATE_LIMITED (429): suggest switching to small test model or add exponential backoff snippet in example
- TIMEOUT (504): recommend increasing timeout in example client and show how to configure global timeout via SDK config
- NON_DETERMINISTIC_SNAPSHOT: note: generation nondeterminism means snapshots should use seeded small models only

UX edge cases / notes to self:
- Hooks: include `--no-telemetry` flag for privacy-concerned customers; default ON for internal pilots
- Tokens: show per-call token estimate in sample output to highlight cost-awareness
- Windows: provide PowerShell equivalents for env setup (quick note in README)
- Networking: if user behind corporate proxy, add tiny troubleshooting section: `HTTP_PROXY`/`NO_PROXY`

Rollout checklist (who does what):
- eng-devx: add pilot-lite folder + scripts + CI (owner: Emma)
- docs: add short page in developer portal and link from SDK README (owner: Alex K)
- growth/solutions: include 1-pager for SEs to run with customers (owner: Priya)
- infra: create sandbox API key pool and GH secret name (owner: Mateo)

Unresolved questions / tradeoffs:
- Should telemetry be opt-out or opt-in for external pilots? (Privacy/regulatory angle)
- Do we enforce a strict sandbox quota per repo? how to rotate keys for public forks?
- Snapshot testing: do we include golden outputs in repo or generate on the fly in a curated fixture?

Linked tickets and immediate todos:
- DEVX-431: create sandbox key rotation + GH secret standard (see linked_artifacts)
- DEVX-2148: telemetry ingestion shape work (needs mapping to backend events)
- PR: github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/812 (example changes waiting review)

Next steps (short term):
- Ship pilot-lite directory behind feature-flaged README and CI (2 days)
- Quick internal demo for SEs + collect feedback (end of week)
- Iterate telemetry contract with backend (small schema update)

Notes to self (scratch):
- Keep samples extremely short: one file per language, max ~25 LOC for core example
- Avoid creating platform-specific dependencies in pilot (no docker required)
- Consider a tiny playground page (static) that runs the same sample via ephemeral key for discovery

Slack channels / people to ping: #devx, @alex.kim, @priya.nair, @mateo.ruiz

——
This file is intentionally lightweight (brain-dump + checklist). Move to a formal PR-ready doc after the first pilot validates the flow.
